newsitem.title: USA: Rivlin says unclear if U.S. economy slowing enough.
newsitem.headline: Rivlin says unclear if U.S. economy slowing enough.

text.p: Federal Reserve Vice Chairman Alice Rivlin said Wednesday the economy was slowing from its unsustainable first quarter pace but it was unclear if it would slow to a sustainable rate.
Rivlin said in an interview with Public Television's Nightly Business Report that it was a "close call" on whether the Fed should take steps to slow the economy.

"I'm not sure exactly how I feel right now about what we ought to do in July," Rivlin said of the Fed's next policy-setting meeting "but what we will be weighing is the risk of future inflation against the desirability of waiting a little longer and seeing what happens."
The U.S. economy grew at a robust 5.8 percent annual rate in the first quarter of the year.
"The economy in the first quarter was certainly growing faster than was sustainable. We don't exactly know what's sustainable. We certainly know that it's not 5.8 percent," Rivlin said.
"It's slowing down now. Will it slow down enough so that it settles at a sustainable rate? Nobody's quite sure," she said.
Rivlin said the economy had shown over the past year or so that unemployment could be a good deal lower than 5.5 percent without accelerating inflation.
"But we have to make sure we keep it up," she said.
The Labor Department reported last week that the unemployment rate had dropped to 4.8 percent in May from 4.9 percent in April.
Rivlin said she was optimistic that the economy had taken some difficult steps that were now paying off, such as improving corporate efficiency and reducing the federal deficit.

"It's possible that if we are very careful and very lucky that this good growth and low unemployment can continue without inflation for a good many years," Rivlin said, adding, "we just can't be sure of that.
Rivlin said that based on past behaviour there was reason to be worried about inflation.

"So what the Federal Reserve has to weigh, is the economy growing so fast or will it grow so fast that we should take steps to slow it down and make sure that inflation doesn't rear its ugly head, or should we wait for a little bit more information."
